solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What could cut more than half of this puzzle?

indicators.note: taking more than half of a word means keeping most of it and dropping the opening part

parts.note: the puzzle you are solving is a crossword

explanation.surface: A teasing question about what could slice through most of today's grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five of the nine letters of CROSSWORD give SWORD, which is more than half.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed weapon, something that could indeed cut.

clue.text: Drinks up in a fit of anger

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: fortified wines from Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone drinking heavily while in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is informal British slang for a sulky bad temper or tantrum.

clue.text: Old road — one terribly neat line on chart?

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched, so these letters come out in a messed-up order

parts.note: standard abbreviation for old
standard abbreviation for road
the Roman numeral for one
the letters of neat rearranged

explanation.surface: An old road with one badly tidy line drawn on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinate is the vertical coordinate on a graph, a line or value read off the y-axis.

clue.text: Refutation Daniel has been rewritten

indicators.note: a name that has been rewritten is set down again differently, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: A refutation of what Daniel said has been redrafted.
explanation.definitionFit: A denial is a statement contradicting a claim, which is what a refutation is.

clue.text: Pointer dogs run around ring

indicators.note: the letters before it are placed around the following item, holding it inside

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs
cricket scoring abbreviation for run
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Pointer dogs racing round a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' looks like the dog breed in this doggy surface, but it is the definition. CURS plus R wraps round the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursor is the movable marker on a computer screen showing where you are pointing.

clue.text: Deer took cover around centre of spinney

indicators.note: the word for hiding goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to take cover is to hide; past tense

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter only

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters

explanation.surface: A deer hiding in a small wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinney is a British word for a small wood or copse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hind is a female deer, especially of the red deer.

clue.text: Under Scottish mountain take in first of heather

parts.note: ben is the Scots word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
to take in food is to eat

indicators.note: the first of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: Beneath a Highland peak, taking in the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath and under are synonyms meaning in a lower position than something.

clue.text: Choice of former clues I have written with an E missing

indicators.note: says outright that one letter E is to be dropped from what was written

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
taken as written
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A setter boasting of a choice set of old clues, one with a typo.
explanation.walkthrough: The E dropped is the one in CLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, choice and exclusive both mean select or high-class, open only to the few.

clue.text: Ending of short illness

parts.note: curt means brief or short in manner
an ailment is a minor illness

explanation.surface: The close of a brief bout of sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtailment is a cutting short, the bringing to an end of something.

clue.text: Fuss in Royal Navy making radioactive gas

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the abbreviation that follows

parts.note: standard abbreviation
ado means fuss, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A commotion in the navy over a gas leak.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, element 86.

clue.text: Remainder live outside university

indicators.note: the verb for living sits outside, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An instruction for the leftover students to live off campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remainder after the rest is removed.

clue.text: Enclose worker carrying new flag

indicators.note: something carrying another thing holds it within itself

parts.note: to pen animals is to enclose them
a worker ant; ant is the usual crossword worker
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A command to fence in an employee who is bearing a fresh banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enclose' and 'worker' join first; the new letter then sits inside the combined pair, not inside one of them alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennant is a long tapering flag, as flown on ships.

clue.text: Let the wine breathe — did it come from a duty-free here?

definitions.text: did it come from a duty-free here?

wordplay.note: letting wine breathe is airing it, and the wine is port

explanation.surface: A sommelier opening a bottle and wondering if it was bought tax-free on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction reads as two words, air port, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free shops are found at an airport, so it is the place the bottle may have come from.

clue.text: Stage work to repeat all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A show staged to be performed again everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera, a musical work performed on stage.

clue.text: Universal worship gives lift

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing
to praise God is to worship

explanation.surface: Worship by everyone raises the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is to raise up or lift, a slightly archaic verb.

clue.text: Win purse I've avidly wanted regularly

indicators.note: wanted means lacking, so letters are missing at regular intervals and every other one stays

parts.note: first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone eager to win a cash prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win through or triumph.

clue.text: Keenly very into daily working

indicators.note: working means in operation, so the word is set to work in a new arrangement
one piece goes into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters of daily rearranged
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone very enthusiastic about their everyday job.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes after the A of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Avidly and keenly are synonyms meaning eagerly or with enthusiasm.

clue.text: University lecturer embraced by one French female is ruined

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held within its arms

parts.note: French for one in the feminine
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: An academic's downfall through an affair with a Frenchwoman.
explanation.definitionFit: Undone, in its old sense, means ruined or brought to destruction.

clue.text: Time ran out for mosque's construction

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A building project at a mosque ran out of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower that forms part of a mosque.

clue.text: Recurring theme in pupil's assessment overturned without resistance

indicators.note: something overturned is turned upside down, which in a down entry reads it backwards
without means lacking, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: a school report assesses a pupil
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A teacher's report gets reversed after a complaint about a recurring point.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a recurring motif or device in literature or film.

clue.text: Sign of gold turmeric, say

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
turmeric is an example of a spice, flagged by 'say'

explanation.surface: Golden turmeric read as an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen or sign, originally one read from the flight of birds.

clue.text: Dispatched SAE, not empty

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: SAE is a stamped addressed envelope; keep its ends
keep the ends

explanation.surface: A stamped addressed envelope that was posted but did not arrive empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not empty' looks like a phrase about the envelope, but 'not' is a word to empty too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent and dispatched both mean sent off, as of a letter.

clue.text: Go better than alfresco party

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An outdoor party that tops the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo is to surpass, doing better than a rival.

clue.text: Only one to turn informer twice

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police
a second slang way to turn informer: let on, reveal a secret

explanation.surface: A lone criminal who grasses twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a single individual, the only one rather than one of a pair or group.

clue.text: Avoid Adam being half grabbed by his partner

indicators.note: something grabbed by another is held inside its grip

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner in Genesis

indicators.note: half a word keeps only one of its two halves, dropping the rest

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Adam dodging Eve's half-hearted embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or escape something by cleverness.
